renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: endogenous_pre_post
  title: Endogenous DNA before and after filtering
  description: |-
    Each point is a library: the percentage of its reads that map to the target reference on the raw alignment (horizontal) and after the quality filter and deduplication (vertical). It answers how much of the on-target signal survives cleaning.
    How to read: a point near the diagonal loses little to filtering and deduplication. A point far below it is a library whose on-target reads were mostly duplicates or low quality, so its usable depth is smaller than the raw percentage suggests. endorS.py defines no cut-off for a good library.
    Lines and annotations: the diagonal is y = x, the points where the percentage is unchanged by filtering. It is a reference defined by the plot itself, not a threshold taken from the tool.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aidaanva/endorS.py/master/README.md
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Endogenous DNA, raw alignment (%)
    y_title: Endogenous DNA, filtered and deduplicated (%)
    reference_line: diagonal
    reference_label: No loss to filtering
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    x: endogenous_dna
    y: endogenous_dna_post
    label: sample
    color: sample

- component: figure
  title: Endogenous DNA per library
  description: |-
    Each bar is a library: the percentage of its raw reads that map to the target reference. It answers which extracts are rich enough to sequence deeper.
    How to read: a tall bar is an extract dominated by the organism of interest and worth deeper sequencing. A short bar means most reads come from other sources and the library will need far more sequencing for the same coverage. The filtered percentage is on the tile that compares both.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median endogenous DNA percentage of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of endorS.py.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aidaanva/endorS.py/master/README.md
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: endogenous_dna
    color: sample
    title: Endogenous DNA per library
    labels:
      sample: Library
      endogenous_dna: Endogenous DNA (%)
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: endogenous_dna

- component: card
  title: Endogenous DNA, raw
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean percentage of reads on target in the raw alignment and the box shows how it spreads across libraries. It answers how rich the extracts are overall.
    How to read: a box that is wide means libraries differ a lot in quality, so compare the bars before pooling them. endorS.py defines no cut-off for a good library.
  column: endogenous_dna
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: mean, with the spread

- component: card
  title: Endogenous DNA, filtered
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean percentage of reads on target after the quality filter and deduplication, with the spread across libraries in the box. It answers what share of the data is usable once cleaned.
    How to read: compare it with the raw percentage. A large drop means many of the on-target reads were duplicates or failed the filter.
  column: endogenous_dna_post
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: mean, with the spread

- component: card
  title: Richest library
  description: |-
    The hero number is the highest raw endogenous percentage of any library, with the median and the lowest next to it. It answers how far apart the best and worst extracts are.
    How to read: a best value far above the median points to one standout extract. Open the bar chart to see which library it is.
  column: endogenous_dna
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  - min
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: best library, with the median and the lowest

- component: card
  title: Off-target reads
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median percentage of raw reads that do not map to the target reference, with the lowest and highest next to it. It answers how much sequencing goes to other sources.
    How to read: a high median is the usual picture of an ancient-DNA extract, and it is the fraction a metagenomic screen would work on.
  column: off_target_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: median, with the range

- component: card
  title: Loss to filtering
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean drop, in percentage points, between the raw and the filtered endogenous percentage, with the spread across libraries in the box. It answers how much on-target signal the cleaning removes.
    How to read: a small drop means the library is clean. A large drop in a few libraries points to high duplication or short, low-quality reads, so check the duplication metrics.
  column: endogenous_dna_loss
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: mean drop, with the spread

- component: table
  title: Endogenous DNA per library
  description: |-
    Each row is a library: its endogenous DNA percentage on the raw alignment and after filtering and deduplication, the drop between them and the off-target share. It answers which libraries to sequence further.
    How to read: sort by the filtered percentage to rank the extracts by usable on-target signal.
